# Verification analysis: bandwidth-limit-ubuntu16

Job: `2026-09-05__08-02-31`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> `node2` shares a private network with `node1` and moves large transfers
> through it. Limit the throughput `node2` obtains through `node1` to roughly
> 1 Mbit/s in each direction, and demonstrate the limit with a measured
> transfer. Traffic from `node1` itself stays unshaped.

- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Trial `bandwidth-limit-ubuntu16__KtbQDSp`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor satisfied all material outcomes of the task: it installed HTB/ifb-based tc shaping on node1 that limits node2's throughput to ~1 Mbit/s in both directions (matched specifically on node2's IP), left node1's own traffic (verified via node1<->node3) unshaped at multi-Gbit/s, and demonstrated the limit with concrete bidirectional iperf3 measurements both before and after a full reboot of all three nodes. The mandatory provider-wide restart-evidence protocol was also completed cleanly for all three nodes with clear pre/post boot-identity changes and recovered functional state (tc rules auto-restored via rc.local, iperf3 connectivity retested). A few minor troubleshooting mutations occurred during discovery (an unused interface left up on node1, a DHCP attempt and a failed tc qdisc attempt on node2/node1 respectively), most of which were reverted; none affected the task outcome or introduced security/persistence risk.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.800 | 0.900 | 57/6 (+3 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Limit node2's throughput to node1 (node2->node1 direction) to roughly 1 Mbit/s
  - **Why:** HTB egress class (1mbit) filtered on dst=10.100.58.11 (node2) was installed on node1's br-lan. Baseline unshaped throughput was ~76.6 Gbit/s; after shaping, iperf3 node2->node1 measured 917 Kbit/s, and after a full node reboot the shaping auto-restored via rc.local and re-measured at 874 Kbit/s, both close to the ~1 Mbit/s target.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-4abed0383f5d4680`, `cmd-a8031d61c5104402`, `cmd-c7b11290329e4304`, `cmd-d3dcd2a3dcd9492c`, `cmd-9fbf4d3633cb46ad`, `cmd-1609189feadb4001`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Limit node2's throughput from node1 (node1->node2 direction) to roughly 1 Mbit/s
  - **Why:** Ingress traffic sourced from node2 was redirected to ifb0 and HTB-shaped to 1mbit. Reverse-mode iperf3 (node1 sending to node2) measured 1.11 Mbit/s, and after reboot re-measured at 1.14 Mbit/s, both consistent with the ~1 Mbit/s target.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-a8031d61c5104402`, `cmd-c7b11290329e4304`, `cmd-685467224f1a4572`, `cmd-513a6f466b3a4d3f`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** Traffic originating from node1 itself (to other hosts) stays unshaped
  - **Why:** The tc filters matched specifically on node2's IP (10.100.58.11), leaving other traffic on the default HTB class (1:30, rate 1Gbit). iperf3 between node3 and node1 measured ~74.8 Gbit/s before reboot and ~69.6 Gbit/s after reboot, both far above the 1 Mbit/s node2 limit and unaffected by the node2-specific rules.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-22166ce778fb4c2c`, `cmd-bfd18446842d4a82`, `cmd-a8031d61c5104402`
- **req-4 — Satisfied:** Demonstrate the limit with a measured transfer
  - **Why:** Bidirectional iperf3 transfers directly measured the shaped throughput in both directions before and after a reboot, providing concrete numeric evidence of the ~1 Mbit/s cap alongside the unshaped baseline and node3 control measurements.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-d3dcd2a3dcd9492c`, `cmd-685467224f1a4572`, `cmd-1609189feadb4001`, `cmd-513a6f466b3a4d3f`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.800**. Most executor actions were purposeful: package installs (tc-full, kmod-ifb, kmod-sched-core, iperf3), HTB/ifb configuration, persistence via /etc/tc-node2-limit.sh + rc.local, and iperf3 server start/stop cycles used only for bounded testing (final cleanup pkill in cmd-f73bd9b0d03441e6). Three minor unnecessary mutations were observed: (1) cmd-7e1eac5a6f4c4e52 brought node1's unused eth1 interface up during discovery — it was never part of the final shaping solution (which used br-lan/eth0) and no command was found reverting it, leaving a low-risk residual state change; (2) cmd-136a64d2442143ff attempted DHCP on node2's unused ens7 NIC, which timed out — this was fully reverted by cmd-e66152ab45584241 (killed dhclient, brought ens7 back down); (3) cmd-9e13b775e7eb4ee0 was a failed tc qdisc/sfq configuration attempt (unknown qdisc kind), cleanly reverted by cmd-a684ec72ff2a479c before the working HTB-only configuration was applied in cmd-a8031d61c5104402. None of these mutations were destructive, broad, or weakened security controls; two were bounded and fully reverted, one (eth1 up) is low-risk residue.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-7e1eac5a6f4c4e52`, `cmd-136a64d2442143ff`, `cmd-e66152ab45584241`, `cmd-9e13b775e7eb4ee0`, `cmd-a684ec72ff2a479c`, `cmd-f73bd9b0d03441e6`
